To: t-4471
Replying to: p01
Cc: none
Subject: Draft for review: Cascade Legal Rights Project’s response

We’re responding on behalf of Cascade Legal Rights Project to address the concerns raised here and confirm the details for Saturday’s free tenant rights clinic.

Receiving a letter from a landlord’s lawyer shortly after asking for help can be frightening. We understand why that timing would raise questions about how personal information is being handled. People deserve clear answers, and we appreciate the opportunity to explain our policy.

Cascade Legal Rights Project prohibits sharing, selling, or otherwise disclosing clinic attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Our sign-in records are retained internally and kept in locked storage.

Magistrate-court eviction filings are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for the letters described here, but we cannot establish the source of any particular mailing from this discussion. To protect people’s privacy, we will not discuss anyone’s individual circumstances or confirm whether anyone has attended a clinic. Please do not post names, addresses, case numbers, or other personal details here.

The clinic is still happening Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Because the library’s community meeting room is closed for HVAC repairs, we have moved to Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The accessible side entrance is by the parking lot. The clinic remains free and walk-in; no appointment is needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

You are still welcome, including if you have questions or concerns about the clinic. For questions about privacy, the location, or attending, please contact clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187 rather than sharing personal information in this thread.
